cross_references.label: ERISA Fiduciary Duties — The Underlying Breach
cross_references.note: §1113 governs the limitations period for claims arising from §1104 fiduciary duty violations. The breach of the prudent expert standard and exclusive benefit rule are the substantive claims; §1113 governs when they must be filed.

cross_references.label: ERISA Fiduciary Personal Liability — The Remedy
cross_references.note: §1109 claims (make plan whole; disgorge profits) are subject to §1113. The limitations period for recovering plan losses caused by the unauthorized retirement election runs under §1113.

cross_references.label: ERISA Civil Enforcement — Plan Recovery
cross_references.note: §1132(a)(2) suits to recover plan losses under §1109 must be filed within §1113's limitations period. The two-track structure applies to all §1132(a)(2) fiduciary breach actions.

cross_references.label: ERISA Benefit Recovery — Separate Limitations Period
cross_references.note: §1132(a)(1)(B) benefit recovery claims (to receive benefits wrongly withheld) may have a different limitations period — courts apply ERISA's analogous state limitations periods. §1113 applies to fiduciary breach claims, not necessarily to pure benefit recovery claims.

cross_references.label: Ongoing Breach Doctrine — SOL Clock Anchor
cross_references.note: Each failure to review and correct a plan status is a new breach under Tibble. The 6-year long-stop runs from the last such failure, not the initial unauthorized election. Any administrative act treating the fraudulent status as valid restarts the clock.

cross_references.label: Actual Knowledge Standard — Discovery Rule
cross_references.note: Actual knowledge means the plaintiff actually knew of the breach — constructive notice is not enough. A participant who received documents but was never told that an unauthorized retirement election was processed does not have actual knowledge from the documents alone.

cross_references.label: ERISA Minimum Vesting — Nonforfeitable Rights
cross_references.note: §1053 rights are nonforfeitable — an unauthorized election cannot extinguish vested benefits. A plan's ongoing refusal to correct the fraudulent status may constitute an ongoing breach of both §1104 and §1053 simultaneously, with the §1113 clock running from the most recent refusal.
